title: Pitch template part 3: team, scalability, requirement and exit
summary: The closing slides of the pitch: why your team is best suited, when, where and how you scale, how much you need and for what, and your exit, plus the full slide order.

chunks.heading: Team Competency
chunks.explanation_md:
**Team Competency: Why you are best suited to solve this problem.**

The slide asks for two things about your team:
- **Qualification & Professional Experience**
- **Something interesting about you or your team**

It links back to the problem: you are showing why *your* team is the one best suited to solve *this* problem.

key_terms.meaning: Why you are best suited to solve this problem: qualification & professional experience, and something interesting about you or your team.

chunks.heading: Scalability: when, where, how
chunks.explanation_md:
The **Scalability** slide has three prompts:

- **When**
- **Where**
- **How: Promotion Plan**

The "how" of scaling is your **promotion plan**.

chunks.heading: Requirement and Exit
chunks.explanation_md:
The last two content slides are short.

**Requirement**:
- **How much**
- **For what purpose**

**EXIT**:
- **When**
- **How much X**

So you state how much you need and what it is for, and then when you would exit and how much X.

key_terms.meaning: How much you need, and for what purpose.

chunks.exam_line: Requirement: how much, for what purpose. Exit: when, how much X.

clarification.text: the point at which founders or investors sell their stake and take their money out of the business.

chunks.heading: The whole pitch in order
chunks.explanation_md:
Put together, the very early stage pitch runs in this order:

- Problem Statement
- Solution
- Market Size
- Competitive Landscape
- Customer Segment(s)
- Insight
- Uniqueness / Unfair Advantage
- Business Unit Economics
- Revenue Streams
- Team Competency
- Scalability
- Requirement
- EXIT

A simple way to hold it: **problem and solution**, then **market and customers**, then **why you win**, then **how you make money**, then **who you are**, and finally **growth, the ask and the exit**.

questions.stem: Differentiate between the Requirement slide and the EXIT slide of the pitch template.
questions.model_answer_md:
Both are short closing slides, but one is about what you need now and the other about how it ends.

| Basis | Requirement | EXIT |
|---|---|---|
| Prompts | How much; for what purpose | When; how much X |
| Looks at | What the startup needs | When and at what X the exit happens |
| Position | Second last content slide | Last content slide |

So Requirement states the ask, and EXIT states the way out.

rubric.point: Requirement: how much, for what purpose
EXIT: when, how much X
Ask now versus way out later

questions.stem: What does the Scalability slide of the pitch template ask for?
questions.model_answer_md:
The Scalability slide has three prompts about growing the startup.

- **When:** the timing of scaling.
- **Where:** the places it will scale to.
- **How: Promotion Plan:** how it will be done, through a promotion plan.

So scaling is pitched as a timed, located and promoted plan.

questions.stem: List and explain the slides of the very early stage pitch template in order.
questions.model_answer_md:
The template is a **startup pitching template for a very early stage** venture. After a cover with the **Startup NAME** and **what you aspire to do**, it has thirteen content slides, in this order.

**Problem and solution**
- **Problem Statement:** the problem that you intend to solve.
- **Solution:** unique feature, significant advantage, major benefit, value proposition, and what's new and what people are forced to do now.

**Market and customers**
- **Market Size:** Total Available Market and Target Market at Stage I.
- **Competitive Landscape:** a heading to fill in.
- **Customer Segment(s) that we serve:** key characteristics, pain points and goals.

**Why you win**
- **Insight:** what you understand that others just don't know.
- **Uniqueness / Unfair Advantage:** why it would be hard for others to duplicate what you do.

**How you make money**
- **Business Unit Economics:** average cost and average revenue per transaction.
- **Revenue Streams:** strategies, not projections (pay-per-use, subscription, licensing); when commercial sales begin, total five year revenue estimate, at a cost of.

**Who you are**
- **Team Competency:** why you are best suited; qualification and professional experience; something interesting about the team.

**Growth, ask and exit**
- **Scalability:** when, where, how (promotion plan).
- **Requirement:** how much, for what purpose.
- **EXIT:** when, how much X.

In short: problem and solution, market and customers, why you win, how you make money, who you are, then growth, the ask and the exit.

questions.stem: Your team has members from BCom, Computer Engg, BBA with design and content writing skills, and HR. Using the Departmentation table from the list of business ideas, fill in the Team Competency slide of the pitch template.
questions.model_answer_md:
The Team Competency slide asks **why you are best suited to solve this problem**, with **qualification and professional experience** and **something interesting about the team**. The Departmentation table shows which competence fits which department.

**Qualification mapped to departments**

| Member's competence | Department they lead |
|---|---|
| BCom | Finance |
| Computer Engg | Website |
| BBA, Design Skills, Content writing | Digital Marketing and Business Development |
| HR | Scheduling, Record Keeping and Journalling |

**Why best suited**
- Every department the handout names has a member with the matching competence.
- **Operations** is left blank in the table, so the team should state who covers it.

**Something interesting about the team**
A mix of commerce, engineering, management and HR backgrounds in one student team.

**Link to the model**
This also completes Stage 1, **form team and delegate operations**, of The MBA Entrepreneurship Model.

So the slide shows a team whose qualifications match each job the business needs.

Digital Marketing and Business Development: BBA, design, content writing
Scheduling, record keeping, journalling: HR; Operations blank
